plan.english: Lords, hear my word! Three strangers arrived in the night and drove off our cattle. What shall we do? Shall we go to war, or shall we send them gifts? Then a lord stood up and spoke: "If we send gifts, they will come again. Let us strike them down, and let us win good fame! Who of you is afraid? I am not afraid!" "Let us ask them. If they do not listen to me, then we shall go. Who will bring my word to them?" "I shall bring it."

Listen to me, lords! A king bringing gifts and a bride price has come from the hill. He asks for my daughter. Is he friendly, or a stranger? Then a lord spoke: "Give her! Then he will be your son-in-law, and a son-in-law does not strike his own father-in-law." Then a lord said: "Do not give your daughter to him! Who knows his heart?" "Now I speak: let him sit at my fire and drink water, and let him give me a pledge. And my daughter will be his. Father Sky, see this pledge! May he be friendly to us, and may he not be a wolf!"

Brothers, a king is coming on ten swift horses. Where shall we stand? Then a lord said: "Let us stand on that hill. The hill guards us, and horses do not climb it." "Whoever sits on it wins no fame. Trembling will seize them. Let us strike them at dawn! Let us go down into the field! Father Sky, give us great fame!"

Brothers, my brother has sent me word: "Come! A king is striking me." Then a lord said: "We have a settlement and bulls. Let us not go." Then a lord spoke: "A brother's war is ours. If he dies, they will come to us." "I shall go. Who will follow me?" "I shall follow you." "Mother Earth, protect my brother! May he live, and may they fall!"

Fathers, my ten warriors have seized the young son of the king. What shall we do? Shall we kill him, or shall we set him free? Then a lord said: "Kill him! A young wolf grows up, and then he eats the sheep." Then a lord spoke: "Do not kill him. Whoever dies is no friend." "Let us set him free. Let his father bring us gifts, and let us be friendly."

Fathers, five men are standing at our settlement. They ask us for water. Shall they be our guests? Then a lord said: "Our cattle are not many." Then a lord spoke: "Whoever strikes a guest, the gods kill him. Let them sit down at our fire, and let them eat and drink. May they come as strangers and go as friends!"

Brothers, the winter is coming. Shall we go to war now? Then a lord said: "If we go, we strike them down. If we sit, the snow kills us. They will grow cold." Then a lord spoke: "Snow lies on our field. Who will feed our cattle?" "We shall stay and feed them. When the snow melts and the sun grows warm, we shall go. Our fame will be great!"

title: The son asks for the troops

plan.english: Father, hear me! I am young, and I do not fear. Let me lead the troops! "Son, you are young. I have seen nine fights." "Your fame will guard him. My horse will carry him. Let him go!" "Go, my son, and set a famous name! May you come, and may I see you!"

Fathers, you know that pledge. The king of the hill made a pledge to us, and he has broken it. What shall we do? "The gods will strike them. Let us stay." "The gods see the pledge, and the arm of man strikes. Let us be the arm of the gods! Fire, burn them! Let us go!"

Brothers, a hero stands yonder, and he cries: "Let a man come forth to the fight!" Who of you will go? No one speaks. They tremble. Then a young man stood up: "I shall go. I do not fear." "He has killed ten men." "I shall go." "Go, then, and win good fame! May Fire protect you!"

I slew the serpent! Who are you? My arm is swift and my heart is great. Come forth! If you overpower me, seize my horses. If I overpower you, the dogs and wolves will eat you. "You speak many words. My arm will speak. Whoever dies, imperishable fame will remain to him."

title: The king's son and the shepherd

plan.english: Shepherd, who are you? Who is your father? "My father is a king and he is famous. Guard your sheep!" "I am a shepherd. A wolf seized a sheep; I struck it with my arm. I am not afraid of it; am I afraid of a man? Strike me, or go away! A man dies; a famous name does not die."

Hear me! Two swift horses carry me. The wheel of the sun is bright. I put the yoke on my team at dawn, and no one follows me. Come to my field! Dawn, daughter of Sky, look on us! "Swift horses will not save you. My arm will seize you, and your wheel will break."

Your words are many. I have seen many winters, and I know war. A young horse does not know the yoke. Seven young men came to this field, and now they lie there. I am not afraid of you. Go to your mother! Or dwell, and learn the fight.
Dog, you stole my cattle in the night! You are no hero. Come! Dogs will eat you. Run! "I am a dog, and I guard the sheep. You are a wolf. Last year you drove off my cattle. Now I shall seize them!"

Serpent, you devoured my cattle and you devoured my brother! Come forth from your hill! I am not afraid of you. Father Sky, you gave me power! I shall split you. Sun, look at the serpent! "Who are you? Ten men came to me. I devoured them, and I shall eat you." "Then imperishable fame will be mine!"

I am standing. I did not flee from anyone, and I shall not flee from you. Whoever flees wins no fame. Whoever stands in the fight sets a famous name. "I am standing too. Mother Earth, take hold of him who falls!"
My brother and I are standing. Our father is a lord. We two killed wolves; we two are not afraid. Give us our cattle, or we two shall strike you down. "We are many. You are two men."

title: Sky, Earth and Sun as witnesses

plan.english: Hear me! May there be no war between us. I give you swift horses; give me bulls. Let us give a pledge. Father Sky, listen to us! Mother Earth, listen to us! Sun, listen to us! Fire, listen to us! Whoever breaks this pledge, may his own fame die! "I listen to you. My pledge is yours."

Lord, I have overpowered you. Your fame is good. Your men and mine lie yonder. Let us leave this fight, and let us drink water! Give me ten horses, and I shall be your friend. "I give them." Gods, givers of good things, see this pledge!

I have a daughter. Let your brother be my son-in-law. Give a bride price. "I give the bride price. I send gifts and seven bulls. May she be dear to my brother." Dawn, lead her home! Sun, see this pledge! May they be dear!
I know you. Your father was a guest of my father. Let us not go to the fight! We two are guests to each other. Let my gift be yours, and your gift mine. Let us sit by this fire.

Lord, let the hill be yours, and the water mine. The field lies between us. Let your bulls drink at my water, and let my sheep eat in your field. "Your word is good. Let it be so." The sun goes, and the earth stands. May our pledge stay!

title: A pause to burn the dead

plan.english: Hear me! Those who fell lie yonder. Let us burn them with fire, and let us cry for them. "Give me a pledge." "I give it." Fire, listen to us!

title: The man who asks for his brother

plan.english: Lord, I have come bringing gifts. Give me my brother! Remember your father! "Sit down, and eat and drink. I give you your brother. The gods led you to me."

Your man killed my brother. Bring me ten bulls: that is my brother's payment. If you bring them, I shall be your friend. If you do not bring them, I shall go against you. "I listen to you. I bring the bulls." May the pledge stand between us!

Father, I go to war. Do not cry for me. If I die, my name will be famous, and you will say it. If I live, I shall come to my home again. My horse dwells with you. May you live many winters! "Go, my son. May the gods give you great fame, and may they protect you."
Mother, you nourished me. I am not afraid. My three brothers are coming. Do not tremble for me! I shall set a famous name for you. Earth, protect her! May you be well, and may you see me!

title: To his wife at the door

plan.english: Wife, nourish our son. Let our fire be bright. Do not cry. If I do not come again, your husband's brother will protect you. Earth, may you give her good things!
Husband, go, and come again. May Fire go before you, and may your arm grow strong. I shall sit by our fire, and at dawn I shall look for you. Dawn, daughter of Sky, lead him home! Remember me.
Go! Father Sky is the giver of good things; may he give you great fame. May you not be afraid. Do not flee from the fight. Grow strong! May Dawn shine for you! Remember your father!
You go away, and I shall stay. Wear this clothing, which I made for you from my wool. From the hill I shall keep looking at you. May Fire go before you! May the sun be warm for you!
Father and mother, hear me. I go, and my brother dwells with you. Guard my wife. If I fall, do not cry. Burn me. May you live!
Wife, hear me. I leave you my field and sheep. Nourish our daughter. When she is grown, give her to a lord. If I live, I shall come again. If I fall, say my name to her. May she be well!
You have come again! Where did you go? "I went by ship." What did you see? "I saw seven settlements." Are you carrying gifts? "I am carrying gifts for you." Sit down. My heart has become joyful.
You have come. Where is your brother? "He lies yonder. He fell." Did he stand, or did he flee? "He stood. He did not flee." Imperishable fame will remain to him, and my heart cries.
Do you live? "I live." Is your fame great? "My fame is not great. I have come." My heart has become joyful. Sit by our fire, and drink water.
Brother, you have come! You have been gone nine winters. We said: "He was lost." Our mother cried for you. Now I see you, and my heart has become joyful. "I am well. I dwelt in a settlement yonder."

Shepherd, you have come. Where are the sheep? "The sheep are yonder." What did you see in the night? "I saw a wolf. It came to them. The dog and I drove it away." Were you afraid? "I was not afraid." Sit down, and drink water.
Who are you? I do not know you. "Father, I am your son." My son is gone. "I am well. You set a name for me." Speak! I know your word. My heart knows you.
